title: Coproducts of flat module sheaves are flat
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, and let $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ be the category of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. If $(\mathcal M_b)_{b\in B}$ is a set-indexed family of flat sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], then the coproduct $\coprod_{b\in B}\mathcal M_b$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ is flat over $\mathcal O$.

source.place: Lemma 18.28.5 (Tag 03EU), clause (2), direct sums of flat sheaves of modules are flat

proof.text: The universe hypotheses implement [def-weil-size-convention]: C is already a small category. Use the Grothendieck-abelian assertion of [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], directly provided by the proved source theorem SheafOfModules.isGrothendieckAbelian in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.Abelian. The additional generator assertion of that node is not needed. Install the symmetric monoidal structure of the sheaf tensor product and the closed structure of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], directly provided by SheafOfModules.monoidalClosed in WeilConjectures.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.MonoidalClosed. Neither the K-injective resolution theorem nor the full tensor-Hom naturality statement is needed.

For each b, [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] gives exactness of tensorRight (M b), hence preservation of finite limits. Transport it to tensorLeft (M b) using the inverse of BraidedCategory.tensorLeftIsoTensorRight. In this closed category, ObjectProperty.flat_iff_preservesFiniteLimits gives abstract ObjectProperty.flat (M b): colimit preservation follows from closure. These are the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-coproduct].

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-coproduct] to M and the abstract flatness proofs from step 2. Its conclusion includes exactness of tensorRight of the coproduct, via ObjectProperty.flat.tensorRight; this is definitionally [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. No nonemptiness or finiteness assumption on B is used, so the empty coproduct is included.
